test_title: PYST 5: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Two cars start simultaneously from points A and B, 120 km apart, and meet after 2 hours. If the speed of one car is 50 km/h, what is the speed of the other?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = Total Distance ÷ Time = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h

In opposite direction, Relative Speed = Sum of individual speeds

Speed of other car = Relative Speed − Speed of first car

Speed of other car = 60 − 50 = 10 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between **Point A** and **Point B** = 120 km

Time taken to meet = 2 hours

Speed of first car (S₁) = 50 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

When two objects move towards each other, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de4811fc81b694fa314e1615cac486a4041a2bdecaae40a92a0bca80d188df79.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the second car be S₂ km/h.

⇒ Relative Speed = 120 ÷ 2

⇒ Relative Speed = 60 km/h

⇒ S₁ + S₂ = 60

⇒ 50 + S₂ = 60

⇒ S₂ = 60 − 50

⇒ S₂ = 10 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When moving in the **opposite direction**, relative speed is the sum (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (|S₁ − S₂|).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

For a journey with two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p
